easy.q: Who does the psalmist ask to save him?
By what does the psalmist ask God to save him?

easy.explanation: He says, “Hear my prayer, O God.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to hear?

medium.explanation: He asks God to “judge me by thy strength.”
medium.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do after saving him?
What does “give ear” mean in this passage?

answers: The psalmist asks for help and then asks to be heard
The psalmist describes a feast and then a battle
The psalmist offers a sacrifice and then praises enemies
medium.explanation: The first verse asks for salvation and judgment, while the second asks God to hear his prayer.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the two verses?

challenge.explanation: Both verses directly appeal to God for help and attention.
challenge.q: What does the repeated address to God show about the psalmist?

answers: The psalmist seeks both deliverance and righteous judgment
The psalmist asks to become an enemy
The psalmist asks to stop speaking
challenge.explanation: He asks for rescue and for God’s strength to determine his case.
challenge.q: What contrast appears in the requests “save me” and “judge me”?

answers: From asking for salvation to asking for attentive hearing
From praising enemies to fearing God
From making an offering to seeing victory
challenge.explanation: The psalmist first asks for deliverance and judgment, then for God to hear his words.
challenge.q: What is the main movement of thought in these verses?

paragraphs.title: A Plea for Salvation and Attention

easy.explanation: The verse says, “strangers are risen up against me.”
easy.q: Who has risen up against the psalmist?
Who does the psalmist say is his helper?

answers: People who persecute or trouble others
medium.explanation: Oppressors are people who trouble or persecute someone.
medium.q: What does “oppressors” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “they have not set God before them.”
medium.q: What have the enemies failed to do?

answers: God is declared to be his helper
medium.explanation: After describing his enemies, he affirms that God is his helper.
medium.q: How is the psalmist’s danger answered in the next verse?

answers: Enemies seek the psalmist’s soul, but God helps him
Enemies worship God, but the psalmist rejects Him
The psalmist offers a sacrifice, but God refuses it
challenge.explanation: The verses contrast hostile enemies with God’s support.
challenge.q: What contrast is emphasized in these verses?

answers: They act without regard for God
They are asking God for mercy
challenge.explanation: The enemies disregard God in their actions.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “they have not set God before them” suggest?

answers: It shows that God supports the psalmist through His care and protection
It says that God has abandoned him
It identifies the enemies as his helpers
challenge.explanation: The second phrase further expresses God’s supportive presence.
challenge.q: What does “the Lord is with them that uphold my soul” add to the statement “God is mine helper”?

paragraphs.title: Enemies and Confidence in Divine Help

easy.explanation: The verse says, “He shall reward evil unto mine enemies.”
easy.q: What will God do to the psalmist’s enemies?

easy.explanation: He asks, “cut them off in thy truth.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do to his enemies?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the Lord is with them.”
easy.q: Who is with those who uphold the psalmist’s soul?

medium.explanation: The psalmist asks that the evil they have done come back upon them.
medium.q: What does “reward evil unto mine enemies” mean?

medium.explanation: The phrase expresses a request for the enemies’ destruction or removal.
medium.q: What does “cut them off” mean in this context?

answers: He trusts that God is his helper
medium.explanation: Even under threat, he declares his confidence in God’s help.
medium.q: How does the psalmist respond to the threat of his enemies?

answers: The enemies pursue evil, while God provides help and justice
The enemies offer sacrifices, while God refuses to listen
The psalmist fears God, while the enemies trust Him
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts the enemies’ evil with God’s support and righteous judgment.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in these verses?

answers: It connects the judgment with God’s faithfulness and righteousness
It means the enemies will be forgiven immediately
It shows that the psalmist does not believe God
challenge.explanation: The request for judgment is placed in the context of God’s truth.
challenge.q: Why is the phrase “in thy truth” significant?

answers: Threat, confidence in God’s help, and a request for justice
Praise, sacrifice, and confession of sin
Escape, silence, and celebration by the enemies
challenge.explanation: The psalmist describes the threat, affirms God’s help, and asks for righteous judgment.
challenge.q: What progression appears across these verses?

easy.explanation: He says, “I will freely sacrifice unto thee.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist promise to do freely?

easy.explanation: He says, “I will praise thy name, O LORD.”
The verse says, “he hath delivered me out of all trouble.”
easy.q: What has God delivered the psalmist from?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes a willing or freewill offering.

answers: Because it is feared by enemies
medium.q: Why does the psalmist praise God’s name?

medium.explanation: He bases his praise on God’s deliverance.
medium.q: What evidence does the psalmist give for his thanksgiving?

answers: The psalmist witnessed God’s judgment on his enemies
The psalmist never saw what happened
challenge.explanation: The statement indicates that he personally saw the outcome concerning his enemies.
challenge.q: What does “mine eye hath seen his desire upon mine enemies” communicate?

answers: They combine a willing offering, praise, deliverance, and witnessed justice
They remove all mention of God’s help
They focus only on the enemies’ strength
challenge.explanation: The psalmist responds to deliverance with worship and testimony.
challenge.q: How do the final verses strengthen the theme of thanksgiving?

answers: Deliverance leads to sacrifice, praise, and testimony
Fear leads to silence and defeat
Enemies lead to rebellion and abandonment
challenge.explanation: Because God delivered him, the psalmist promises worship and declares what he has seen.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence of thought in these verses?
